clock_and_reset_waveform.SCK: Driven by master baud-rate generator; idle polarity per CPOL; 16 edges per 8-bit byte.
clock_and_reset_waveform.RESET_behavior: After reset SPE=0; SPI disabled; all output pins released to module-default state.

spi_clock_format_0_cpha0.description: First SCK edge is a half SCK cycle after SS goes LOW. Data sampled on odd-numbered edges (1, 3, ..., 15); shifted on even (2, 4, ..., 16). After the 16th SCK edge, shift register contents are transferred into SPI Data Register and SPIF is set.
spi_clock_format_0_cpha0.ss_required_between_transfers: In slave mode the SS line must be deasserted for at least one minimum idle time (~half SCK cycle) between successive transfers for SPI Data Register contents to be transmitted; otherwise the last received byte is re-transmitted.
spi_clock_format_0_cpha0.ss_master_behavior_with_ssoe: Always deasserted and reasserted between successive transfers for at least the minimum idle time.

spi_clock_format_1_cpha1.description: First SCK edge issued by setting CPHA=1 at start of the 8-cycle transfer. First edge commands slave to transfer first data bit to MISO. Data sampled on even edges (2, 4, ..., 16); shifted on odd (1, 3, ..., 15). SS may remain LOW between successive transfers (back-to-back). SPIF set one half SCK cycle after the last SCK edge.
spi_clock_format_1_cpha1.back_to_back_transfers: If a new data byte is available in SPIDR when a transmission completes, it is sent out immediately without a trailing and minimum idle time.

timing_parameters.tL: Minimum leading time before the first SCK edge (not required for back-to-back transfers in CPHA=1).
timing_parameters.tT: Minimum trailing time after the last SCK edge.
timing_parameters.tI: Minimum idling time between transfers (minimum SS HIGH time; not required for back-to-back transfers in CPHA=1).
timing_parameters.guarantee: tL, tT, tI are guaranteed for master mode and required for slave mode.

bit_transfer_waveform.rule: Data on SDA must be stable while SCL is HIGH (data valid window). SDA may change while SCL is LOW (change-of-data window).
bit_transfer_waveform.figure: Figure 4 — Bit transfer on the I2C-bus

start_stop_waveform.start_S: SDA HIGH→LOW transition while SCL HIGH
start_stop_waveform.stop_P: SDA LOW→HIGH transition while SCL HIGH
start_stop_waveform.repeated_start_Sr: Same as S; keeps bus busy without intervening P

data_transfer_waveform.byte_unit: 8 data bits + 1 ACK clock = 9 SCL pulses per byte
data_transfer_waveform.ack_position: On the 9th SCL pulse; receiver pulls SDA LOW
data_transfer_waveform.figure: Figure 6 — Data transfer on the I2C-bus

timing_parameters_high_speed_mode.drive: Open-drain with current-source pull-up; SDA push-pull on HIGH

clock_stretching_waveform: Slave holds SCL LOW after a byte to extend the byte period; master enters wait state.
arbitration_waveform: While SCL HIGH, each master compares SDA actual to SDA driven; master that drove HIGH while bus is LOW loses arbitration immediately.
synchronization_waveform: SCL = wired-AND of all masters' SCL outputs; final LOW period = longest LOW, final HIGH period = shortest HIGH.

clock_waveform.TCK_role: Test Clock. Generated by the tester. Free-running while a scan is in progress; may be stopped or stretched between scans (the FSM holds its current stable state when TCK stops).
clock_waveform.rising_edge: TMS and TDI are sampled here. TAP FSM transitions on this edge. Capture / shift-update of IR and selected DR happen on this edge.
clock_waveform.falling_edge: TDO is updated here so that the next device in the daisy chain sees a stable TDI on the following rising edge of TCK.
clock_waveform.frequency_range: Typical 10-50 MHz at the chip level; lower (1-10 MHz) over backplanes and long board chains. Implementation-defined per device.

tms_tdi_tdo_waveform.TMS_role: Drives FSM transitions; latched on rising edge of TCK.
tms_tdi_tdo_waveform.TDI_role: Shift-in data for IR (in ShiftIR) or selected DR (in ShiftDR); latched on rising edge of TCK; LSB first.
tms_tdi_tdo_waveform.TDO_role: Shift-out data for IR (in ShiftIR) or selected DR (in ShiftDR); driven on falling edge of TCK; LSB first.
tms_tdi_tdo_waveform.TDO_3state_rule: TDO is in the high-impedance state in all FSM states except ShiftIR and ShiftDR. This lets multiple devices' TDOs be combined externally without contention (although daisy-chain usage avoids this entirely).

reset_waveform.TMS_reset_sequence: TMS=1 for 5 consecutive TCK rising edges from any state forces TestLogicReset.
reset_waveform.TRST_asynchronous_reset: TRST=LOW (when implemented) forces the TAP FSM to TestLogicReset immediately, independent of TCK.

ir_scan_waveform_summary: TMS=0 → CaptureIR (1 TCK): IR parallel-loaded with b...b01 pattern.
TMS=0 (N times) → ShiftIR: shift N-bit IR LSB first via TDI; previous IR contents emerge LSB-first on TDO (falling edges).
TMS=1 → UpdateIR (1 TCK): new IR contents become the current instruction on the falling edge.
TMS=0 → RunTestIdle (or TMS=1 → SelectDRScan to start a DR scan immediately).
dr_scan_waveform_summary: TMS=0 → CaptureDR (1 TCK): selected DR parallel-loaded with its capture value (BSR captures pins; Bypass captures 0; IDCODE captures hard-wired ID; user DRs per definition).
TMS=0 (M times) → ShiftDR: shift M-bit DR LSB first via TDI; previous DR contents emerge LSB-first on TDO.
TMS=1 → UpdateDR (1 TCK): shifted DR is parallel-latched (e.g. EXTEST drive values reach output pins on the falling edge of TCK).

rows: Implementation-defined; typical 20-100 ns at chip level.
TDO output delay from TCK fall
timing_parameters_per_device.notes: IEEE 1149.1 does not specify absolute values; per-device datasheets do. Across-chain skew is limited by the slowest device + board interconnect; testers typically run TCK well below each device's worst-case maximum.

mdio_signal_timing.MDIO_TA_high_Z_window_clauses: Read transactions only; first TA bit must be high-Z on both ends, second TA bit driven 0 by PHY

frame_waveform.transmit: TX_EN ↑ on first preamble nibble → TXD shifts 7×0x55 + 0xD5 + DA + SA + Type/Length + Payload + Pad + FCS nibble-by-nibble → TX_EN ↓ on next TX_CLK after final FCS nibble → IFG (96 BT) before next TX_EN ↑.
frame_waveform.receive: PHY raises CRS as soon as line activity is detected → RX_DV ↑ aligned with first preamble nibble (or sometimes within the preamble) → RXD streams preamble + SFD + DA + ... + FCS → RX_DV ↓ before next RX_CLK after final FCS nibble → CRS ↓ shortly after.
frame_waveform.collision_half_duplex: (half-duplex only) During TX_EN, COL asserts as soon as the PHY detects a colliding signal; MAC immediately switches TXD to a 32-bit JAM pattern, then de-asserts TX_EN. After backoff slots, retry from TX_DEFER.

auto_negotiation_waveform.Acknowledge_propagation_pages: At least three identical Base Pages with Acknowledge bit set

transmitter_eye_reference_per_phy: MDI compliance eyes are specified per PMD clause: Figure 14-9 for 10BASE-T, Figure 25-? for 100BASE-TX, Figures 40-19..40-28 for 1000BASE-T. RJ-45 MDI return loss / NEXT specifications are also per PMD clause.
general_timing_rule: All MII / GMII signals are synchronous to TX_CLK (TX path) or RX_CLK (RX path); MDC is asynchronous. Bit times scale linearly with line rate (100 ns at 10 Mb/s, 10 ns at 100 Mb/s, 1 ns at 1 Gb/s); inter-frame gap = 96 BT and slot time = 512 BT (10/100 Mb/s) or 4096 BT (1 Gb/s) are both expressed in bit times so the same MAC FSM scales across the speed range.

clock_and_data_waveform.sample_edge: MDIO sampled on MDC rising edge
clock_and_data_waveform.turnaround: MDIO reverses direction during the 2-bit TA field (Z0 on read)

symbol_directionality.note: MDIO has no break/inter-byte symbols; the on-wire symbol set is the logic-1 bit (H1) and logic-0 bit (H0), one per MDC rising edge.

rx_timing.description: Host (STA) drives the command portion (PRE/ST/OP/PHYAD/REGAD) and samples MDIO on the MDC rising edge during a READ frame. Per-bit widths the DUT/PHY RX decoder must tolerate at 2.5 MHz.
rx_timing.sample_edge: MDIO sampled on MDC rising edge

tx_timing.description: DUT-side drive: STA drives PRE/ST/OP/PHYAD/REGAD + WRITE data + the write-TA; the PHY/MMD drives the TA bit-2 zero and the 16-bit read data MSB first. Per-bit widths the TX encoder emits at 2.5 MHz.
tx_timing.direction: DUT/PHY -> bus (internal, out of the DUT)
tx_timing.drive_edge: MDIO updated on MDC falling edge, stable at rising edge
